input:
An amine absorption unit was tested at pilot scale using gas obtained from a cement kiln, and the unit successfully captured 89% of the carbon dioxide contained in the treated gas. The test was conducted over a period of 45 days at a rate of 11 t of carbon dioxide per day. The steam demand was 3.1 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, while the solvent loss amounted to 2.1 kg per tonne captured. It is important to note that the capture figure and the two consumption figures all describe the same 45-day run, and each figure is expressed per tonne captured in order to allow the run to be compared with other campaigns on a consistent basis.

The main limitation of the test is its duration. Beyond 45 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent remains untested, and the reported capture and consumption figures cannot simply be extended beyond the test period. The figures produced by the unit are pilot figures: they establish what the solvent and the unit were able to achieve on kiln gas over the test period and at the stated rate. Any scale-up exercise will use these figures as a starting point, with the dust question still open and unresolved.

An amine absorption unit tested at pilot scale on gas from a cement kiln captured 89% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas. The test ran for 45 days at 11 t of carbon dioxide per day. Steam demand was 3.1 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, and solvent loss was 2.1 kg per tonne captured. The capture figure and the two consumption figures describe the same 45-day run, and each is stated per tonne captured, so the run can be compared with other campaigns on the same basis.

Stated per tonne captured, the steam demand prices the separation in energy terms and the solvent loss prices it in material terms; the two figures together describe the running cost of the capture at the rate tested, before any allowance for the capital of the unit itself. The capture percentage, the steam demand and the solvent loss were all measured on the same gas over the same period, so the three figures belong to one another and are not to be combined with figures from other campaigns.

The limit of the test is its duration. Beyond 45 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent is untested, and the reported capture and consumption figures are not extended past the test period. The figures are pilot figures: they fix what the solvent and the unit achieved on kiln gas over the test period, at the stated rate, and a scale-up starts from them with the dust question open.
